meta.probingQuestion: When you crack, what's the first thing that shows?
meta.connection: The checkpoint where a guard always breaks is a tell, and so is the first thing that shows when you crack. Finding the exact break point on the mat is the same skill as knowing your own tell.
meta.takeaway: Tonight you worked from a single leg, open guard, and a chest-to-chest pin. Every guard has an exact point where it breaks, and so do you. Finding that point is the same skill as knowing the sign you give off, so you can catch yourself before it runs the show.

slides.title: When you crack, what's the first thing that shows?

body.text: This is a takedown to one leg.

items: The attacker wins when the defender touches the mat with his hips or hands.
The defender wins by freeing his own leg from the attacker's grip.

body.text: This is passing the legs from on top.

items: The top player wins by touching both of the bottom player's knee pits with his own leg, feet off the mat.
The bottom player wins by making the top player sit down, then sitting up himself.

body.text: This is holding someone down by his elbows.

items: The top player wins by keeping the bottom player's elbows away from his body the whole time.
The bottom player wins by bringing both elbows to his body, or making the top player fall.

slides.title: What made it work?
slides.question: You've got both hands locked around your partner's leg, and he's trying to pull away. What's the smart move?

options.text: Keep moving him while staying on the leg.
options.feedback: Staying attached while he moves is the same as noticing the sign you give off before it runs the show.

options.text: Let go of the leg and reset your stance.
options.feedback: Letting go here gives the leg back for nothing.

options.text: Freeze in place and grip as hard as possible.
options.feedback: Keep moving him instead of freezing.
